_description: Planetary absorption-band database for p.matter.bands. Wavelengths in micrometres (µm). band_depth method: left/center/right shoulder wavelengths for continuum-removed depth. Entries are science-backed; DOIs listed.

mars._notes: Mars surface and atmosphere. Ehlmann & Edwards 2014 (Annu. Rev. Earth Planet. Sci.) is the primary review.

absorption_bands.note: Shift toward shorter λ with increasing SiO2 content
Broad suspended dust emission; TES dust opacity
TES LWIR dust spectral index region
CO2 combination band; overlaps silicate — use caution

moon._notes: Lunar surface mineralogy dominated by mafic silicates and plagioclase. Space weathering creates nanophase iron reducing band depths. Pieters et al. 2009 (Science) confirmed OH/H2O.

absorption_bands.note: Weak Fe2+; often absent in pure anorthosite
Fe2+-Ti4+ charge transfer; reduces UV albedo
Broad Fe2+ in glass; much broader than crystalline pyroxene

ices.name: water_ice
ices.context: Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs) at poles; also thin OH layer at all latitudes

mercury._notes: Mercury has extremely low FeO content (<2 wt%). Dark material is graphite. Sulfur-bearing minerals (CaS, MgS) are unique to Mercury. MESSENGER XRS/VIRS data. Nittler et al. 2011.

absorption_bands.note: Darkens UV; no sharp feature, low albedo across full range
Tentative; laboratory spectra show shoulder ~0.5-0.6 µm
Very weak due to low FeO; detection marginal from orbit

venus._notes: Venus surface observed only through NIR atmospheric windows (1.02, 1.10, 1.18, 2.26, 2.3 µm). Atmosphere opaque elsewhere. EnVision/VenSpec will open UV window (0.2-0.4 µm). Hashimoto & Sugita 2003.

absorption_bands.note: NIR atmospheric window; lower emissivity = older/tesserae terrain
1 µm surface window + MERTIS-V; extreme surface T ~735 K
~50 % contrast at 0.36 µm in cloud tops; candidates: FeCl3, S3, OSSO, chlorine-based
Shifted from H2O 1.37 µm; D/H ratio diagnostic of Venus water history
Cloud particle size diagnostic; 75–85 wt% H2SO4
2.3 µm surface window; thermodynamic proxy for lower atmosphere

titan._notes: Saturn's largest moon. Dense N2/CH4 atmosphere. Surface organic sediments and hydrocarbon lakes. Cassini VIMS (0.35-5.1 µm) primary data source. Clark et al. 2010.

absorption_bands.note: Strong UV absorption slope; Khare et al. 1984 lab spectra

ices.name: water_ice
ices.context: Bedrock material; rare surface exposure beneath organic sediments

absorption_bands.note: Ice phase; shifted from gas-phase 3.01 µm
Cassini/VIMS window around 4.78 µm surface channel
Ice phase; detected by Cassini/VIMS near poles
Specular reflection / low emissivity; Stofan et al. 2007

europa._notes: Jupiter's icy moon. Ocean world. Irradiation products from Jovian magnetosphere modify surface. Europa Clipper/MISE (0.8-5.0 µm) will provide hyperspectral mapping. McCord et al. 1998 (Nature) foundational.

absorption_bands.note: Color centers from irradiation; Trumbo et al. 2019

ices.name: h2o_ice_mir
ices.display_name: H2O ice (MIR) — libration and phonon bands

absorption_bands.note: Structurally bound OH in amorphous SiO2
Key Hand & Carlson 2007 band; overlaps with sulfate
JWST NIRSpec detection Trumbo et al. 2022; endogenous ocean salt
Fe2+ crystal-field transition; diagnostic of endogenous iron brine

io._notes: Jupiter's volcanic moon. SO2 frost dominates. Sulfur allotropes produce distinctive UV-VIS colors. NIMS (Galileo) primary spectral data. Future: JUICE/MAJIS.

absorption_bands.note: S2 / polysulfides absorb blue-UV; causes Io's yellow/orange color

ices.name: s2_disulfur
ices.display_name: S2 (disulfur) — lava lake hot spot gas

absorption_bands.note: Schumann-Runge-like UV-VIS band system; Hubble/HST detectable
Responsible for yellow-orange surface colour; variable with temperature

enceladus._notes: Saturn's plume-active moon. Nearly pure H2O ice surface. Plume contains H2O, CO2, CH4, H2, organics. Cassini VIMS/CIRS primary data. Future: proposed Enceladus orbiter.

ceres._notes: Largest asteroid / dwarf planet. Ammoniated phyllosilicates detected by Dawn VIR. Water ice at Oxo crater. Occator bright spots are NaCl/hydrated carbonates. De Sanctis et al. 2015 (Nature).

absorption_bands.note: N-H stretch of NH4+; diagnostic for Ceres

ices.name: water_ice
ices.context: Oxo crater (fresh exposure); subsurface ice layer inferred

asteroid_c_type._notes: Carbonaceous chondrite parent bodies. Hydrated silicates, organics, dark carbon. Key missions: Hayabusa2/Ryugu (Kitazato 2019), OSIRIS-REx/Bennu (Hamilton 2019).

absorption_bands.note: Fe2+/Fe3+ charge transfer; 0.7-µm drop; diagnostic for C-types
Featureless UV reddening; diagnostic of C-complex vs. D-type
C-H stretch; detected on Ryugu samples (Yabuta et al. 2023)

asteroid_s_type._notes: Stony (ordinary chondrite / LL) parent bodies. Dominated by olivine+pyroxene+metal. Space weathering reduces band depth. Itokawa (Hayabusa) paradigm case.

comet._notes: Cometary nuclei and comae. Organics dominant on surface (Capaccioni et al. 2015 for 67P/VIRTIS). Ices sublimate to form coma. Future: Comet Interceptor (2029 launch).

absorption_bands.note: Aromatic C-H + other C-H; dominant in 67P VIRTIS (Capaccioni 2015)
O-H stretch; coma emission at 2.65-2.73 µm
Strongest UV tracer of water outgassing rate; parent of H and O
Brightest coma emission outside OH; photodissociation of HCN
Photodissociation product of CS2; abundant in bright comets

pluto._notes: Dwarf planet / KBO. New Horizons LEISA (1.25-2.5 µm) revealed complex volatile ice distribution. CH4 > N2 > CO > CO2 > H2O. Grundy et al. 2016 (Science).

absorption_bands.note: Very weak; N-N stretch 2nd harmonic; detected in Tombaugh Regio
UV absorption drives tholin formation; Lyman edge photolysis products
Bright terrain salt residue from ocean brine migration

ices.name: so2_frost_trace
ices.display_name: SO2 frost trace (Io plasma torus fallout)

absorption_bands.note: Implanted from Io's plasma torus; near-polar concentrations
Organic-rich lag; featureless UV-VIS slope + 3.4 µm C-H
Strongest CO2 band of any Galilean moon; trailing/pole enhanced
Most surface area; broad low-albedo component
Very sharp; temperature-sensitive position (α↔β phase 35.6 K); best volatile thermometer
Shifted from pure CO by N2 matrix; Triton and Pluto diagnostic
Broad absorption causing pink colour of polar cap

ices.name: co2_ice_ariel
ices.display_name: CO2 ice (very strong — Ariel's defining feature)

absorption_bands.note: Strongest CO2 signature of Uranian moons; trailing hemisphere
JWST NIRSpec confirmed; endogenic vs exogenic origin debated
Associated with smooth, young cryovolcanic resurfacing
Mixed in with ice; likely irradiation products + carbon
Very weak or absent in D-types; olivine Band I
Pyroxene Band II — diagnostic if present
Featureless red slope from 0.4–2.5 µm; steeper than C-types
Lucy/LEISA target: aliphatic organics on Leucus/Polymele
Aromatic organics; Emery et al. 2011 Trojan detection
Detected in ~20 % of outer-belt D/P-types; aqueous alteration
